articles.title: About Personalisation Hub
articles.summary: What Personalisation Hub is, the 3 product areas it covers, and the benefit each feature delivers — the executive summary for a new customer.

articles.title: Benefits by industry
articles.summary: What Personalisation Hub delivers for retail, retail media, telco, banking, hospitality, grocery and pharmacy, venues and automotive, with a first use case for each.

articles.title: Use cases supported by Personalisation Hub
articles.summary: The 3 primary use cases — connected retail experience, first-party retail media targeting and hyper-localised QSR campaigns — with links to the articles that set each up.

articles.title: Your first 30 days: the recommended set-up order
articles.summary: The 11 milestones a new customer follows, in order, from the pre-installation checklist to reviewing insights — who does each and roughly how long it takes.

articles.title: Pre-installation checklist
articles.summary: Every decision, account, key and asset to gather before installing Personalisation Hub, grouped by when it is needed, with the 3 permanent choices flagged.

articles.title: Glossary
articles.summary: Alphabetical definitions of the terms used in HQ Admin, Retail Admin and this help centre, from AI agents and display types to zones.

articles.title: Where is my data stored and how is the platform secured?
articles.summary: Your data stays in your own AWS account and VPC. How it is stored and encrypted, who can reach the platform, how users and integrations authenticate, and what you retain.

articles.title: How do I get support?
articles.summary: Raise a ticket at the help centre or email support, and include your platform domain, environment and identifiers so the issue is resolved faster.

articles.title: Is there a free trial?
articles.summary: Yes — the AWS Marketplace subscription includes a 30-day free trial of the licence, cancellable at any time; AWS infrastructure costs are billed separately.

articles.title: Install Personalisation Hub from AWS Marketplace
articles.summary: Deploy Personalisation Hub into your own AWS account in six stages — a little over an hour end to end, with about 7 minutes of hands-on set-up.

articles.title: Step 1 — Deploy the platform through AWS Marketplace
articles.summary: Subscribe in AWS Marketplace and create the CloudFormation stack that builds Personalisation Hub in your own AWS account — about 4 minutes to create.

articles.title: Step 2 — Run the Installation Wizard
articles.summary: Create the Master Admin account in the Installation Wizard, choose your environment and platform domain, and install the platform — around 55 minutes.

articles.title: Step 3 — Set up DNS after installation
articles.summary: Add the 2 CNAME records the platform emails you and verify your domain — within 3 days, before the AWS certificate expires.

articles.title: Step 4 — First login and platform set-up
articles.summary: Sign in to HQ Admin for the first time, set a strong password, verify the platform email address with AWS and complete Platform Set-up.

articles.title: Step 5 — Upload your brand, logos and icons
articles.summary: Confirm your brand name and business category, then upload logos and icons for dark and light backgrounds so the platform carries your branding.

articles.title: Step 6 — Add your stores from Google Places
articles.summary: Find your stores in Google Places, add them to the platform and give each one a unique store code so retail staff can be linked to their store.

articles.title: Step 7 — Restrict platform access by IP address
articles.summary: Limit access to your Personalisation Hub instance to approved IP address ranges — offices, VPN, stores and connected platforms — without locking yourself out.

articles.title: AWS deployment: prerequisites
articles.summary: The skills, IAM permissions and DNS arrangements your cloud team needs before deploying and operating Personalisation Hub in your AWS account.

articles.title: AWS deployment: architecture
articles.summary: How Personalisation Hub is built: its microservice components, the AWS services it runs on, and why it uses Kubernetes on EKS.

articles.title: AWS deployment: resources provisioned
articles.summary: The AWS resources the CloudFormation stack and installer create, where data is stored and encrypted, and which endpoints are public.

articles.title: AWS deployment: testing and troubleshooting
articles.summary: Check the 5 points that confirm the Installation Wizard and platform stack deployed correctly, and fix the common failures.

articles.title: AWS deployment: lifecycle management
articles.summary: Licensing, billable AWS services, environment sizes, cost control, quotas, key rotation, patches, upgrades and backups for a deployment.

articles.title: AWS deployment and support guide
articles.summary: The installation timeline, what to include when contacting support, and the standard support response and resolution targets.

articles.title: Company Settings and Platform Admin explained
articles.summary: Learn which settings live under Company Settings, which live under Platform Admin, and which article documents each page.

articles.title: Add HQ Admin, Marketing and Helpdesk users
articles.summary: Invite colleagues to HQ Admin as Admin, Marketing or Helpdesk users from Company Settings → Platform Set-up, and send them their password link.

articles.title: Define target audiences and campaign objectives
articles.summary: Add the target audiences (personas) and campaign objectives that every campaign brief and the AI agents draw on, under Company Settings → Campaign Settings.

articles.title: Upload Retail Admin users for your stores
articles.summary: Create Staff and Store_Manager accounts for every store by uploading a CSV under Company Settings → Retail Admin Set-up, then share the login link.

articles.title: Integrate single sign-on (SAML) for store staff
articles.summary: Let store staff and managers sign in to Retail Admin through your organisation's single sign-on by raising a SAML integration ticket with support.

articles.title: Sign in to the Retail Admin site (no SAML/SSO)
articles.summary: Sign in to the staff tablet (Retail Admin) with your email address and first-time password, then set your own password.

articles.title: Add custom menu links (CTA settings) to HQ Admin and Retail Admin
articles.summary: Add your own links to the HQ Admin or Retail Admin left-hand menu, show or hide the log-out button and back-link, and set the default Retail Admin profile image.

articles.title: I can't sign in to the platform
articles.summary: Work through the 5 most common reasons a Personalisation Hub sign-in fails, from the wrong login page to an expired invitation link.

articles.title: I see an Access Denied error
articles.summary: An Access Denied page means your IP address is blocked, either by the platform's IP restrictions or by your organisation's CDN. Here is how to tell which and fix it.

articles.title: How store data works in Personalisation Hub
articles.summary: Understand what a store record holds, who maintains each part of it, and how it drives localisation, queueing, appointments and connected displays.

articles.title: Add a store
articles.summary: Add one or many stores to HQ Admin from Google Places, then give each a customer-facing name and a unique store code.

articles.title: Update a store code
articles.summary: Change a store's unique code in HQ Admin, and update it in AEM first if AEM is your content management system.

articles.title: Update a store's name
articles.summary: Change the customer-facing name of a store on its Store Details tab in HQ Admin.

articles.title: Add or update a store's address
articles.summary: Add or correct a store's street address, suburb, postcode, state and country on its Store Details tab in HQ Admin.

articles.title: View a store's network and display status
articles.summary: Check each morning which stores have displays offline, using the connected-displays column on the Stores / Branches list.

articles.title: Download a store's QR code for its mobile store site
articles.summary: Download a transparent PNG QR code that opens a store's mobile store site, for use on signage, print and packaging.

articles.title: Delete a store
articles.summary: Remove a store from HQ Admin permanently, and unpublish and delete it from AEM first if AEM is your content management system.

articles.title: Validate your store's details and address (Retail Admin)
articles.summary: Store staff: check and correct your store's address, phone number, website and languages spoken from the Store Profile page on the staff tablet.

articles.title: Update your store's opening hours (Retail Admin)
articles.summary: Store staff: set your store's opening and closing time for each day of the week, mark closed days and set the store time zone on the staff tablet.

articles.title: Set special holiday opening hours (Retail Admin)
articles.summary: Store staff: set different opening times, or no appointment slots, for upcoming public holidays from the Special Holiday Hours tab on the staff tablet.

articles.title: Update your store's segments (Retail Admin)
articles.summary: Store managers: switch your store's variable segments on or off from the staff tablet so localised campaigns start or stop playing in your store.

articles.title: How displays and devices work in Personalisation Hub
articles.summary: Understand what a display is, how it is registered, typed and monitored, and where HQ Admin and Retail Admin let you manage it.

articles.title: Enable digital signage
articles.summary: Turn on digital signage for your organisation and for each store, and get the connection details your devices need before you register them.

articles.title: Register a new display or device
articles.summary: Move a connected device from Unassigned Devices to a named display in a store, with a display type, so it starts receiving campaigns.

articles.title: Create a display type and playlist
articles.summary: Add a display type for a screen orientation and resolution; the platform creates its default playlist for every display of that type.

articles.title: View a display's status and time offline
articles.summary: Filter the Displays & Devices list to offline screens, see how long each has been offline, and open a display's details to diagnose it.

articles.title: Get notified when a display goes offline
articles.summary: Create an offline device notification so the right people receive an email when displays have been offline for a set time.

articles.title: Identify campaign playback issues on a display
articles.summary: Filter the Displays & Devices list to screens with playback issues and open the breakdown of when campaigns stopped playing.

articles.title: Configure campaign playback monitoring
articles.summary: Turn on closed-loop campaign optimisation and set the rules that classify a campaign as on rotation, mark it inactive, and retain playback records.

articles.title: View a display's log history
articles.summary: Open the Device Status tab for a display to see every offline period, disconnection and change recorded against it.

articles.title: View the campaign playback audit for a display
articles.summary: Check which campaigns are on rotation across your displays from the list, then open a display's Campaign Playback tab for the full history.

articles.title: Filter displays by the channel they are playing
articles.summary: Narrow the Displays & Devices list to the screens on a given display type and read the Active Playlist column to confirm which channel each is playing.

articles.title: Rename a display
articles.summary: Change a display's name from HQ Admin or from the Retail Admin staff tablet so it describes where the screen sits in the store.

articles.title: Update a display's image or icon
articles.summary: Replace the picture shown next to a display in HQ Admin and Retail Admin so staff can recognise the screen at a glance.

articles.title: Change a display's screen orientation
articles.summary: Rotate a display's output by 90, 180 or 270 degrees from HQ Admin or the Retail Admin staff tablet; the change applies immediately.

articles.title: Find all the identifiers for a display
articles.summary: Open a display's Display Details tab to copy its Asset ID, serial number, IP address, device ID, make and model for troubleshooting in other systems.

articles.title: Enable QR Control on a display
articles.summary: Turn on QR Control for one display so visitors can scan the code on screen and use their phone as a remote control for its triggered campaigns.

articles.title: Enable chatbot interactions on a display or mobile site
articles.summary: Let a Dialogflow chatbot trigger campaign playback on a display, started either on the display itself or on the visitor's phone.

articles.title: How campaigns work: playback strategies, touch-points and status
articles.summary: Understand what a campaign is made of, what the playback strategy pills and status values on the Campaigns list mean, and what each campaign tab controls.

articles.title: Launch a new campaign
articles.summary: Start a campaign from Launch a New Campaign: describe it to the AI assistant by typing or speaking, or write the brief yourself, then review and save it.

articles.title: Generate storyboard, copy and creative with AI
articles.summary: Turn a saved campaign brief into a storyboard, copy, a preview and production-ready assets for every enabled touch-point, refining each stage as you go.

articles.title: Add a campaign to play on a digital signage display
articles.summary: Connect a campaign to a display through its playlist, upload an image or video for that playlist, and activate it so the display starts playing it.

articles.title: Schedule a campaign
articles.summary: Add 1 or more schedules to a campaign so it plays at set times, on a repeat pattern, or only while each store is open.

articles.title: Target a campaign
articles.summary: Build AND/OR targeting rules on a campaign's Targeting tab so it plays only in the stores, on the displays, or for the audiences that match.

articles.title: Activate or deactivate a campaign
articles.summary: Turn a campaign on or off with the toggle on its detail page, or activate and deactivate several campaigns at once from the Campaigns list.

articles.title: Prioritise which campaigns play first
articles.summary: Set the order in which active campaigns are presented for a display type from the Campaign Prioritisation button on the Campaigns list.

articles.title: Review campaign performance in Insights / Analytics
articles.summary: Read playback, views and engagement for your campaigns by display type and location, and download the raw reports as CSV or JSON.

articles.title: Localise campaigns with store segments
articles.summary: Group stores into fixed or variable segments, assign the segments to stores, and target a campaign at a segment so it plays only in those stores.

articles.title: Target campaigns at specific displays with display tags
articles.summary: Create display tags, assign them to individual displays, and target a campaign at a tag so it plays only on those screens.

articles.title: Localise campaigns by visitors' reason for visit
articles.summary: Play a campaign in a store when more than a set percentage of the visitors waiting in its queue are there for the same reason.

articles.title: Localise campaigns by the skills of staff on shift
articles.summary: Play a campaign only while a staff member who speaks a given language, and is set to Available, is on shift in the store.

articles.title: Target passers-by using computer vision at the edge
articles.summary: Play a campaign when the webcam on a display detects a passer-by of a given gender, with the model running on the device so no images leave the store.

articles.title: What are triggered campaigns?
articles.summary: Understand what a triggered campaign is, what can trigger it, and how it differs from an on-rotation campaign.

articles.title: Update a campaign's interaction settings
articles.summary: Set how long a triggered campaign's pop-up message shows on the visitor's phone and when the display clears the interaction.

articles.title: Enable QR Control and set the default QR code settings
articles.summary: Turn on QR Control so every connected display shows a QR code that visitors scan to choose and play triggered campaigns.

articles.title: Change the QR code size, colour or position on a display
articles.summary: Override the default QR Control settings for 1 display so its QR code fits the screen and the content around it.

articles.title: Let retail staff activate triggered campaigns
articles.summary: Enable the Staff Tablet touch-point so store staff can play a triggered campaign on a display while talking to a visitor.

articles.title: Connect a triggered campaign to an AI agent interaction
articles.summary: Play a triggered campaign on a display when an AI agent or chatbot recognises a visitor's conversational intent.

articles.title: Trigger campaigns from customer or decisioning data
articles.summary: Connect your CDP or decisioning platform to the Visitor API and target triggered campaigns on the data it sends.

articles.title: Use customer and decisioning data to personalise the store visit
articles.summary: How visitor data flows from your CDP through the Visitor API to displays, staff tablets and HQ insights during a store visit.

articles.title: Connect your mobile app or third-party system to the Visitor API
articles.summary: Authenticate your own app or a third-party site with the Visitor API, and pass Store Code and Display ID to it with tokens.

articles.title: Connect AI models and providers
articles.summary: Register your OpenAI, Google Gen AI and LTX API keys under Platform Admin → AI Models / Integrations so the AI assistant can create campaigns, and set retry behaviour.

articles.title: AI agents and skills reference
articles.summary: The AI skills the platform runs when it creates a campaign, what each produces, which model it uses, and the inputs it draws on.

articles.title: Enable proximity personalisation with MIST
articles.summary: Connect your Juniper MIST account, map stores to MIST sites and displays to zones, so displays personalise as a visitor's phone enters a zone.

articles.title: Does computer vision store images of shoppers?
articles.summary: No — the vision model runs on the player at the edge and only anonymous audience attributes are used to target campaigns.

articles.title: Why create a mobile site for your stores?
articles.summary: Learn what a mobile store site is, the 4 visitor states it responds to, and how visitors reach it from QR codes, messages and your app.

articles.title: Define your default mobile site template
articles.summary: Set the header and menu items of the default mobile site template so every store's site covers visitors away from, at, and inside the store.

articles.title: Test your mobile site
articles.summary: Check your mobile store site on a phone in each visitor state by scanning the store's QR code and a display's QR Control code.

articles.title: Add Google Maps directions to your mobile site
articles.summary: Add a Directions menu item that opens Google Maps navigation to the visitor's store, using a token so 1 template works for every store.

articles.title: Create a mobile site template for a concierge kiosk
articles.summary: Create a template with a single Join the queue menu item so visitors who scan the concierge display are taken straight to the queue.

articles.title: Assign a different mobile site template to a store, display or zone
articles.summary: Give a store its own mobile site template, or assign a template to the displays in a zone so the menu changes with the visitor's location.

articles.title: Choose which campaigns appear in the campaign carousel
articles.summary: Control which triggered campaigns a visitor can browse in the mobile site's campaign carousel by enabling the Store Sites touch-point and activating campaigns.

articles.title: Control the order campaigns are presented in
articles.summary: Set the order in which live campaigns appear in the mobile site's campaign carousel for each display type using Campaign Prioritisation.

articles.title: Create a call to action for on-rotation campaigns
articles.summary: Upload an onsite banner and add a call to action button so visitors who scan a display's QR code can act on any on-rotation campaign.

articles.title: Personalise a visitor's store experience
articles.summary: Give visitors a different mobile site menu and campaigns in each zone of a store by creating zone templates and assigning them to the displays there.

articles.title: My mobile site shows a blank page
articles.summary: A menu item or campaign URL loads blank because the destination site blocks framing; switch it to open in a new tab or update the site's CSP.

articles.title: Enable virtual store queueing
articles.summary: Turn on virtual store queueing in Platform Admin, add reason-for-visit categories, upload staff and enable queueing per store — about 15 minutes.

articles.title: Add reason-for-visit categories and sub-categories
articles.summary: Define the reasons a visitor can choose when joining the queue, with a time to serve for each, plus optional sub-categories and visitor-type filters.

articles.title: Queue settings reference
articles.summary: Every field on the Queue Settings tab in Platform Admin → Queueing / Appointments, with its default value and what it controls.

articles.title: Update the platform's SMS sender ID
articles.summary: Replace the default ${BrandName} SMS sender with your own sender ID in Company Settings → Platform Set-up, and check AWS has approved it.

articles.title: SMS and email messages sent to visitors
articles.summary: The 13 SMS and 7 email templates the platform sends to queue and appointment visitors, when each is sent, and how to turn one on or off.

articles.title: Set up a dedicated concierge display or kiosk
articles.summary: Turn a display at the store entrance into a join-the-queue kiosk: a single-item mobile site template plus QR Control on that display — a few minutes.

articles.title: Update your staff profile
articles.summary: Change the first name and last name shown to visitors and colleagues from the Profile page in Retail Admin — under a minute.

articles.title: Update your profile photo
articles.summary: Replace the default initials avatar with a photo that visitors see on their phone when you pick them up from the queue.

articles.title: Manage your availability status
articles.summary: Set yourself Available or Unavailable in Retail Admin so wait-time estimates stay accurate — and know when the platform changes your status for you.

articles.title: Update the languages you speak
articles.summary: Add the languages you speak to your staff profile so managers can route visitors who need them to you via the On Hold queue.

articles.title: Add a visitor to the queue manually
articles.summary: Register a visitor in the store queue from the staff tablet when they cannot or do not want to scan a QR code — about 30 seconds.

articles.title: Let a visitor join the queue by scanning the QR code on the staff tablet
articles.summary: Show the join-the-queue QR code on the staff tablet so the visitor registers from their own phone, using their stored contact details.

articles.title: Let a visitor join the queue by scanning a QR code on a display
articles.summary: Add a join-the-queue option to the mobile site shown by QR Control on store displays, so visitors can join from anywhere in the store.

articles.title: Pick up a visitor from the queue
articles.summary: Take the next visitor from the Waiting view, find them using the notes on their record, and start the visit so the timers and SMS fire.

articles.title: Place a visitor on hold
articles.summary: Pause a visitor without losing their place — to hand them to a colleague with the right skills, or while they step out — and pick them up again from On Hold.

articles.title: Add additional information to a visitor in the queue
articles.summary: Record context on a visitor's queue record so the next staff member knows what they need and the visitor does not have to repeat themselves.

articles.title: See which languages staff on shift speak
articles.summary: Check the languages of an individual staff member, of everyone on shift, or of a store from HQ Admin, before routing a visitor who needs one.

articles.title: Copy a visitor's mobile number or email address
articles.summary: Copy a picked-up visitor's mobile number or email address to the clipboard with one tap, to look them up in your CRM without retyping.

articles.title: View a visitor's recent interactions and profile data
articles.summary: See where a queued visitor has been in the store and what they interacted with, plus any connected customer data, before and after you pick them up.

articles.title: View queue and appointment history
articles.summary: Open the Queue History and Appointment History tables in Retail Admin to see who visited, why, who served them and how long they waited.

articles.title: View store queueing stats and the staff status widget
articles.summary: As a store manager, read the store-wide queueing stats, drill into an individual staff member's stats, and see who is available, serving or unavailable.

articles.title: Remove a visitor from the queue
articles.summary: As a store manager, delete a visitor from the Waiting, In Progress or On Hold view — for example one left over from the day before.

articles.title: Handle visitors with special requests (language or business customers)
articles.summary: As a store manager, move a waiting visitor straight to On Hold with a note or required language, so the right staff member picks them up.

articles.title: Retail Admin shows 'Lost Connection to Queueing Server!'
articles.summary: What the 'Lost Connection to Queueing Server!' banner in Retail Admin means and what to do about it.

articles.title: Enable appointment bookings
articles.summary: Turn on appointments platform-wide, enable them for each store and check your reason-for-visit list so customers can book a time instead of queueing.

articles.title: Appointment template settings reference
articles.summary: Every setting on an Appointment Template in Platform Admin, with its default value and what it controls.

articles.title: Set appointment slots per store and per day
articles.summary: Set how many appointments a store accepts per timeslot on each weekday and on public holidays, from Retail Admin or HQ Admin.

articles.title: Block out dates and times for appointments
articles.summary: Stop customers booking appointments on chosen dates or times by enabling calendar blocking and adding one-off or recurring calendar blocks.

articles.title: Appointment SMS and email notifications
articles.summary: The SMS and email messages the platform sends to customers about their appointments, when each is sent, and the retry and sender settings behind them.

articles.title: Connect the platform to Google Maps / Places
articles.summary: Save your organisation's Google Maps API key under Platform Admin so the platform can find store addresses in Google Places.

articles.title: Obtain your Google Business Profile API credentials
articles.summary: Find the OAuth Client ID and Client Secret for your Google-approved Business Profile project and add the platform's redirect URI.

articles.title: Connect the platform to Google Business Profile
articles.summary: Authenticate Personalisation Hub with your Google Business Profile account and choose which stores to synchronise with the platform.

articles.title: Back up your Google Business Profile data
articles.summary: Download all your store listings from Google Business Profile before you synchronise them with the platform.

articles.title: Create API authentication credentials for an integration
articles.summary: Create a Secret/Token under Platform Admin → API Authentication for each third-party platform that connects to Personalisation Hub.

articles.title: ChromeOS: register a Chromebox with Google CDM and assign your kiosk app
articles.summary: Enrol a Chromebox in Google Chrome Device Management, add the kiosk app in the Google Admin console and set it to auto-launch at start-up.

articles.title: ChromeOS: set up a new organisational unit in Google CDM
articles.summary: Create organisational units in the Google Admin console so every ChromeOS display inherits the right device and kiosk settings.

articles.title: Install the AEM Screens player on Mac or PC
articles.summary: Install the Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Screens player on a Mac or Windows PC for local testing of digital signage.

articles.title: Troubleshooting index
articles.summary: Find the fix for what you are seeing: every symptom-first article in the help centre, grouped by access, set-up, messaging, displays, mobile sites and queueing.

articles.title: SMS messages are not sent or arrive as UNVERIFIED
articles.summary: Queue and appointment SMS messages fail or show UNVERIFIED when your AWS account is still in SMS sandbox mode or your sender ID is not registered.

articles.title: A display shows as offline
articles.summary: A red status dot or 'Offline' on a display means it has lost power or network. Check how long it has been offline, then fix the connection at the store.

articles.title: Adding a store finds nothing in Google Places
articles.summary: If searching for a store under Stores / Branches → Add New Store(s) returns no results, the platform has no working Google Maps API key.
